post.description: Create an account and log straight in (FR-1.1).

Ends the session everywhere: every token issued to this user stops working, including
any copy of the cookie. Works without a valid session too, so logging out never fails.

get.description:
The activity to render. `ActivityOut` has no `solution`, so the answer never reaches the
browser (FR-5.3, NFR-S2). `solved` says whether this student has already answered it
correctly, so the page stops offering hints after a refresh too (#158).

post.description:
Grade a submission by comparison with the stored solution and record the attempt (FR-4.2,
FR-4.5, FR-5.3).

Send `{"submitted": {...}}` in the kind's shape: `{"selected": "<option id>"}` for multiple
choice, `{"order": [...]}` for Parsons, `{"answers": {...}}` for fill-in, and
`{"rows": [{"visitedVertex", "queue", "visited", "order"}, ...]}` for a trace table, one row
per BFS step (graded against the engine, so a trace has no stored solution). A submission in the
wrong shape, or one that answers nothing (no option, line, token, pair, test or row), is 422
and isn't recorded. No student code is executed: `check_activity` compares the submission with
the solution, which stays in this process (NFR-S7).

get.description:
Every hint level this student has already unlocked on this activity (FR-4.4, FR-4.5).

Returns an empty list if they have not asked for any hints yet.

schema.title: Response Get Revealed Hints Api Activities  Activity Id  Hints Get

post.description:
Reveal this student's next hint level, one at a time, and record it (FR-4.4, FR-4.5).

No body. Each call returns the next level (1, then 2, …); once every level has been shown,
or once the student has answered correctly, it is 409. When `nextCountsAsSupport` is true,
warn the student before calling again: a correct answer after hint 3 or 4 counts as "met
with support" (ID document §7.4).

Log something only the browser sees, for the pilot's evaluation (FR-10.1). The server adds
who and when. 404 if the video, checkpoint or segment doesn't exist; 429 past 120 a minute.

get.description:
The breadth-first traversal of the scenario, step by step (FR-6.1).

Computed by the one tested engine so the animation, prediction and trace table agree (FR-6.5).
A scenario the engine refuses (bad start vertex, duplicate vertex, edge to an unknown vertex)
is a 422, since the stored data, not the request, is at fault.

The logged-in student's points total and badges (FR-9.4: private to them). Points come from
the server-side rules table and are never negative; badges are never taken away.

post.description: The app has announced every new badge, so none is announced twice.

put.description:
Hide or show points and badges (FR-9.5). They are still earned while hidden, and the
mastery report is never hidden.

get.description:
The logged-in student's mastery report: each objective's result, whether they are ready
for the lecture, and the review path's progress for each objective module 6 marked "not yet"
(FR-7.3 to FR-7.5).

Worked out from their attempts on every request (app/services/mastery.py), so it always follows
the current rules (FR-7.6). Nothing a client sends can set a result: they change only through
attempts. Only ever the student's own.

The objective's review path: its steps in order, and which the student has answered
(FR-7.5). 404 if the objective has no path; 403 until module 6 marks it "not yet", so the
fresh items stay unseen until the student needs them.

put.description: Choose a profile picture from the team's set, or none (FR-1.6). Only the student sees it.

post.description:
Change the password (FR-1.5). The current one is required, so a session left open on a
shared computer can't be used to take the account over; the new one must pass the same rules
as registration (NFR-S1). Every other session is logged out, and this one carries on.

400 with the reason if the current password is wrong or the new one breaks a rule; 429 after
10 tries a minute.

400.description: The current password is wrong, or the new one is the same or breaks a password rule. `detail` says which.

429.description: More than 10 tries in a minute.

get.description:
All modules with the student's computed status and progress (FR-2).

Returns every module in display order.  ``status`` is one of:
``locked | open | in_progress | complete``.  No commit needed — read-only.

schema.title: Response List Modules Api Modules Get

get.description:
One module with its full ordered segment list and the student's status.

Returns 404 if the module does not exist; 403 if it is locked for this
student (the previous module has not been completed yet).

post.description:
Record the student's current segment position and return the updated module.

The client calls this whenever the student advances to a new segment.
The furthest segment reached is kept, so stepping back changes nothing. A segment must be
done (its activity answered, or its video's checkpoints passed) before moving past it, and
saving the last segment again once it is done marks the module ``complete`` for good (saving
it while it isn't done changes nothing).

Returns the updated ``ModuleDetailOut`` so the frontend can re-render the
module detail page with the new status in one round-trip (consistent with
``submit_attempt`` returning ``AttemptOut``).

Returns 404 if the module does not exist; 403 if it is locked; 409 if the position is more
than one segment past the furthest the student has reached, or past a segment they haven't
done yet.

get.description:
Everything the player needs in one call (FR-3): media and captions paths, the transcript,
and each checkpoint with its activity (without the answer) and whether this student has
passed it. Answer a checkpoint with `POST /api/activities/{activityId}/attempts`.

post.description:
Upload one file to the media volume. Send the raw file as the body, with
`Content-Type: video/mp4` and `?kind=video`, or `Content-Type: text/vtt` and `?kind=captions`.
Returns the `/media/…` path to put in the video. Up to 95 MB for a video, 1 MB for captions.

The exact Content-Type is required: a cross-site form can't send these types, so another
site can't make a logged-in team member's browser upload files.

get.description: Every video, newest first, with how many checkpoints each has.

schema.title: Response List Videos Api Staff Videos Get

post.description:
Create a video with its checkpoints (leave out checkpoint ids). Students see it at
`GET /api/videos/{id}`.

get.description: The video with every checkpoint's question, correct option, feedback and hints.

put.description:
Replace the video and its checkpoint list. Keep each existing checkpoint's `id` so its
attempts stay linked; a checkpoint left out is removed.

schema.title: Response List Members Api Staff Members Get

post.description:
Make the account with this email a team member. It must exist already. Someone who is
staff already stays staff (no error), so pressing the button twice is harmless.

delete.description:
Take staff access away. It ends at once: every request reads `is_staff` afresh. Nobody can
remove themselves, so the portal always has at least one team member left.

get.description: Every account, newest first. The portal searches this list as you type.

schema.title: Response List Accounts Api Staff Accounts Get

get.description:
One account: who they are, totals, progress through each video and their last 10 answers.
What they answered is left out: staff see whether it was right, not the answer itself.

delete.description:
Delete the account and everything stored about it (attempts, hint views, points, badges:
every table of student history, app/services/history.py), in one
transaction. Their session stops working at once: there is no user left to load. Nobody can
delete their own account here.

get.description:
Download one table as CSV for every real student (FR-10.2), oldest first:

- `attempts`: each answer; `submitted` and `detail` are what was answered and the per-part
  result, as JSON.
- `hints`: each hint shown.
- `events`: the timeline (app/services/events.py): videos started and finished, checkpoints
  reached, segments viewed, hints shown, results changing; `payload` as JSON.
- `objective_results`: each student's current result per objective, with the attempts it was
  decided from (`evidence`).

The pilot at a glance (ID document §8.4): per activity, how many students tried it, wrong
attempts, and how many needed hint 3 or 4; per video, how many started it, passed each
checkpoint and finished it, which shows where students stopped. Real students only (no staff
or demo accounts); counts only.

Everything the editor lists: objectives, modules, review paths, activities (not the video
checkpoints' questions), graphs, and the videos a video segment can play.

The content as fixture files (a zip laid out like api/app/seed), to commit to the
repository so a fresh database is seeded with what the portal holds now.

post.description: Add the next objective (up to 8: each has a badge).

put.description:
Change an objective's wording or its mastery rule. Every student's result is worked out
again with the new rule.

Replace a module's details and its segments, in order. Keep each existing segment's `id`;
leave it out for a new one. A segment left out is removed.

delete.description: Delete an empty module made in the portal that no student has started.

409.description: Not possible here; the message says why.

post.description: Add a module after the last one.

put.description: Replace the objective's review path: its segments, in order.

409.description: Not possible here; the message says why.

put.description: Replace an activity and its hints. Earlier attempts keep the result they were given.

409.description: Not possible here; the message says why.

delete.description:
Delete an activity no segment shows. One students have used, or one from the repository,
is taken out of use instead (`deleted: false`).

409.description: Not possible here; the message says why.

post.description: Add an activity. A segment shows it once a module or review path lists it.

delete.description: Delete a graph made in the portal.

409.description: Not possible here; the message says why.

post.description: Drop the portal's edit of this item and load the repository's version of it now.

409.description: Not possible here; the message says why.

AccountAttempt.title: AccountAttempt
AccountAttempt.description: One answer, for the recent-activity list.

AccountSummary.title: AccountSummary
AccountSummary.description: One row of the accounts list.

AccountVideo.title: AccountVideo
AccountVideo.description: Progress through one video: checkpoints answered correctly, out of all its checkpoints.

ActivityInsight.title: ActivityInsight
ActivityInsight.description: How students got on with one activity, as ID document §8.4 analyses it.

ActivityOut.title: ActivityOut
ActivityOut.description:
An activity as the browser sees it. There is deliberately no `solution` field: the answer
stays on the server (SE document §8 "Answers never leave the server").

AttemptIn.title: AttemptIn
AttemptIn.description: A submission: only the student's choices (line ids, chosen tokens), never free-form code.

AttemptOut.title: AttemptOut
AttemptOut.description: The graded result sent back. Carries per-part correctness and messages, never the solution.

AvatarIn.title: AvatarIn
AvatarIn.description: The picture to show, or null for the student's initial.

BfsResult.title: BfsResult
BfsResult.description:
The whole traversal from the start vertex: the final visit order and every step, ready for
the visualiser to animate without further server calls (FR-6.1, NFR-P4).

BfsStep.title: BfsStep
BfsStep.description:
One step of the traversal: the vertex just visited (dequeued), and the state after it
(SE document FR-6.2). `discovered` are the vertices this step added to the queue, in the
alphabetical order they were enqueued; `frontier_edges` are the edges along which they were
discovered (from the visited vertex to each newly discovered neighbour).

CheckpointOut.title: CheckpointOut
CheckpointOut.description:
Where playback stops, and the activity to answer there. `passed` is true once this student
has answered it correctly, so a returning student can seek past it (FR-3.5).

EarnedBadgeOut.title: EarnedBadgeOut

EditorActivityIn.title: EditorActivityIn
EditorActivityIn.description:
`config` and `solution` have the kind's shape (app/schemas/activities.py), exactly as in a
fixture.

EditorDeleteResult.title: EditorDeleteResult
EditorDeleteResult.description:
`deleted`: the row is gone. Otherwise it was only taken out of use (students' answers to
it are kept for the evaluation, FR-10).

EditorSegmentIn.title: EditorSegmentIn
EditorSegmentIn.description:
One step of a module or review path. Leave `id` out for a new one. A `video` segment may
name the video that plays it (`videoId`); the video is made on the Videos page.

EditorVideoChoice.title: EditorVideoChoice
EditorVideoChoice.description: A video a `video` segment can play, and the segment that plays it now, if any.

ErrorOut.title: ErrorOut
ErrorOut.description: An error the client shows as it is: `detail` says what went wrong, in plain words.

EventIn.title: EventIn
EventIn.description:
What the browser saw: `video_started` or `video_completed` (`targetId` is the video),
`checkpoint_reached` (the checkpoint) or `segment_viewed` (the segment).

GraphEdge.title: GraphEdge
GraphEdge.description:
A single edge. For an undirected graph the pair is unordered; for a directed graph the edge
goes from `source` to `target`.

GraphScenarioOut.title: GraphScenarioOut
GraphScenarioOut.description:
A graph scenario as the frontend renders it (FR-6.1): the vertices, the edges, whether it is
directed and where the traversal starts.

HintOut.title: HintOut
HintOut.description:
The hint just revealed. `next_counts_as_support` is true when the *next* hint would be level
3 or 4: show the "this counts as met with support" warning before asking for it (ID doc §7.4).

MasteryReportOut.title: MasteryReportOut
MasteryReportOut.description:
The student's own mastery report. `ready` (for the lecture) is true when every objective is
met, with or without support (FR-7.4). Always shown, even when rewards are hidden (FR-9.5).

MediaOut.title: MediaOut
MediaOut.description: Where the upload is served from. Put it in a video's `mediaPath` or `captionsPath`.

ModuleDetailOut.title: ModuleDetailOut
ModuleDetailOut.description:
A module with its full ordered segment list.

Returned by ``GET /api/modules/{moduleId}``.  Extends ``ModuleOut`` so the
frontend can use the same type for map cards and detail views.

ModuleOut.title: ModuleOut
ModuleOut.description:
A module as it appears on the module map.

``status`` is computed per-student at query time (never stored directly on the
module); it is one of: locked | open | in_progress | complete.
``segment_count`` and ``current_segment_position`` let the map show a progress
bar without loading the full segment list.

ObjectiveReportOut.title: ObjectiveReportOut
ObjectiveReportOut.description:
One objective on the mastery report (FR-7.2, FR-7.3). `answered` of `total` is how many of
its module 6 items the student has answered; the result stays `not_attempted` until all are.
`review` is there once module 6 marks it "not yet", which opens its review path.

PartResult.title: PartResult
PartResult.description:
One graded part: a position in the ordering (Parsons, fix the bug), a blank id (fill-in),
or the index of an item in the config (matching: a left item; choose tests: a test case).

PositionIn.title: PositionIn
PositionIn.description:
Request body for ``POST /api/modules/{moduleId}/position`` (FR-2.5).

The client sends the zero-based position of the segment the student just
reached. The server keeps the furthest one, and refuses a position more than one past it,
so a module can't be finished by jumping to its end.

``ge=0`` rejects negative values at the API boundary: a negative position stored in
``ModuleProgress.current_segment_position`` would cause ``segments[-1]`` (undefined
in JavaScript) on resume, crashing the ModulePage render.

RetrievalActivityOut.title: RetrievalActivityOut
RetrievalActivityOut.description:
A retrieval question the module opens with, before its segments (FR-2.4).

The page loads the question itself from ``GET /api/activities/{id}``, so it is shown like any
other activity, with feedback and hints. ``answered`` is true once the student has made an
attempt at it: the page resumes at the first one still unanswered.

ReviewPathOut.title: ReviewPathOut
ReviewPathOut.description: An objective's review path for the logged-in student (FR-7.5, ID document §7.6).

ReviewProgressOut.title: ReviewProgressOut
ReviewProgressOut.description:
How far the student is through an open review path's fresh items (FR-7.5). Once all are
answered they decide the objective's result, so `answered == total` means the path is done.

ReviewStepOut.title: ReviewStepOut
ReviewStepOut.description:
One step of a review path, in order. An activity step names its activity and its purpose:
`review` is practice with the full hint ladder, `mastery` a fresh item that decides the
result. `answered` is whether the student has submitted an answer to it.

RewardsOut.title: RewardsOut
RewardsOut.description:
The student's own points and badges, and whether they chose to hide them (FR-9.4, FR-9.5).
Only ever the logged-in student's: there is no way to see anyone else's.

SegmentOut.title: SegmentOut
SegmentOut.description:
One segment of a module, in display order.

Kind-specific nullable fields:
- ``body``        — Markdown content, for ``text`` / ``worked_example`` / ``refresher``.
- ``video_id``    — FK to the video, present only for ``video`` segments.
- ``activity_id`` — FK to the activity, present only for ``activity`` segments.

``body``, ``video_id``, and ``activity_id`` are mutually exclusive in practice;
the schema keeps them separate and nullable so the frontend can branch on ``kind``.

StaffCheckpointIn.title: StaffCheckpointIn
StaffCheckpointIn.description:
`id` is set for a checkpoint that already exists (it keeps its activity and the attempts
on it) and left out for a new one.

StaffMemberIn.title: StaffMemberIn
StaffMemberIn.description: Make an existing account staff. By exact email: staff never browse the student list.

StaffMemberOut.title: StaffMemberOut
StaffMemberOut.description: A team member, as the staff portal's "Staff members" page lists them.

StaffQuestion.title: StaffQuestion
StaffQuestion.description: A multiple-choice question. `feedback` says why each wrong option is wrong, by option id.

StaffVideoIn.title: StaffVideoIn
StaffVideoIn.description:
A whole video as the editor saves it. PUT replaces the checkpoint list: a checkpoint left
out is removed. Media paths come from `POST /api/staff/media` and must exist.

VideoInsight.title: VideoInsight
VideoInsight.description:
How far students got through one video: who started it (or answered one of its
checkpoints), who passed each checkpoint and who watched to the end. A drop between two steps
is where students stopped.

VideoOut.title: VideoOut
VideoOut.description:
`mediaPath` and `captionsPath` are same-origin URLs under /media/. Checkpoints come in the
order they are reached.
